headline: Sunny and warm through Friday, with a breezy Kentucky afternoon and increased Friday temperature uncertainty in the Upstate
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Central Kentucky remains sunny and dry through Friday. Deep afternoon mixing and southwest flow support lower- to middle-80s warmth today, while a moisture-starved front turns winds northerly Thursday without producing rain. Clear nights remain locally cool, so verified KDVK and KLEX low-temperature biases are applied to the overnight ranges.

currentConditions.condition: Clear sky inferred from the surrounding complete reports; the latest complete temperature report omitted a text description

days.label: Wednesday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; southwest gusts near 20 mph and afternoon relative humidity around 20–25% may briefly elevate fire spread
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and unseasonably warm. Deep mixing and southwest winds around 5–10 mph, with gusts near 20 mph, should lift most locations into the lower 80s and could allow a few warmer spots to reach the middle 80s. Mostly clear tonight as a dry front approaches; rural locations should cool more efficiently than Lexington.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: No significant weather hazard expected; very low afternoon humidity continues
days.forecast: Sunny and warm behind the weak, moisture-starved front. A light north wind should trim temperatures only slightly, with highs near 80 to the lower 80s. Clear skies and light northeast flow Thursday night favor efficient cooling, especially around Danville and other sheltered rural locations.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No significant weather hazard expected; weekend tropical-remnant rainfall remains beyond this forecast day
days.forecast: Sunny and warm as surface high pressure shifts east. Most locations reach the lower 80s, with the warmest guidance allowing middle 80s. Clouds may begin increasing Friday night, but meaningful rain associated with the Gulf tropical system is expected to hold off until later Saturday or Saturday night.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays sunny and rain-free through Friday, with lower- to middle-80s afternoons and cool rural nights. Today is the breeziest day. The next meaningful rain opportunity arrives after this 72-hour forecast window during the weekend.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather and the overall temperature pattern; moderate-high on exact afternoon highs; moderate on overnight lows because Danville and sheltered valleys routinely cool below broader guidance

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: The Upstate remains dry through Friday. Sunshine supports upper-70s warmth today and a hotter Thursday near the lower or middle 80s. A weak front reinforces northeast flow Friday; current reliable guidance supports a cooler but still mild day, although the size of that cooldown remains the principal forecast uncertainty.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Wednesday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; localized late-night fog is possible near lakes and sheltered valleys
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with light east to variable winds. Highs reach the upper 70s, with warmer locations near 80. Mostly clear tonight; patchy fog may form near lakes and in sheltered valleys, and KLQK-area cold pockets may fall below the Clemson point forecast.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: No significant weather hazard expected; localized early-morning fog remains possible
days.forecast: Sunny and notably warmer beneath the upper ridge. Most locations reach the lower or middle 80s, while the warmest guidance supports upper 80s in favored locations. Winds remain light. Thursday night becomes partly cloudy as a weak front approaches from the north.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; confidence in the daytime high is lower because guidance differs on the strength of cooler northeast flow
days.forecast: Partly sunny and cooler behind a weak front, with northeast winds increasing modestly. The NWS point forecast remains near 81, while the newer ECMWF is near 79 and the GFS is near 76, so the range is intentionally wide. Clouds increase Friday night, but widespread rain should remain west and south of the Clemson area until the weekend.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate remains dry through Friday. Thursday is the warmest day, likely in the lower or middle 80s. Friday turns somewhat cooler under northeast flow, but the exact high remains less certain. More widespread rain is expected after this forecast window over the weekend.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather through Thursday and moderate-high on Thursday warmth; moderate on Friday's high because deterministic guidance spans roughly the middle 70s to lower 80s; moderate on overnight lows because KLQK runs colder than broader guidance

sourceNotes: Official airport observations span 8:15–8:55 AM EDT. KDVK's 8:35 AM report omitted temperature, so its most recent complete temperature observation at 8:15 AM was used. The NWS point forecasts were generated at 6:46–6:50 AM EDT; the Kentucky grid was updated at 6:46 AM and the Upstate grid at 6:25 AM.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:45 AM and 6:34 AM EDT. Louisville supports dry weather through Friday, lower- to middle-80s highs and gusts near 20 mph today. Greenville-Spartanburg supports fair weather through Friday, Thursday warmth and a modest Friday cooldown behind a weak front.

The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either forecast point at the approximately 9:23 AM EDT check. This official alert status is separate from the independent discussion of low humidity, gusty Kentucky winds, localized fog and Friday temperature uncertainty.

Model inventories checked at 9:21 AM EDT showed the complete 06Z HRRR through hour 48, complete 09Z RAP through hour 51, 06Z NAM through hour 84, 06Z NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS and GEFS mean through hour 384, and 06Z ECMWF through hour 144. The partial 12Z HRRR was available through hour 26; incomplete newer cycles were not substituted for complete cycles outside their available ranges.

College of DuPage radar at 9:15 AM EDT showed both forecast regions precipitation-free. Clean-infrared imagery at 9:11 AM EDT showed mostly clear skies across Kentucky and the Carolinas, with the developing tropical system and its deeper clouds confined to the Gulf region.

The earlier apparent Friday Upstate conflict narrowed after the complete 06Z ECMWF became available. The newer ECMWF supports a Clemson-area high near 79°F, GFS guidance is near 76°F, and the NWS point forecast is 81°F. The intentionally wide 75–82°F range represents this remaining but non-material spread, and confidence is reduced accordingly.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

The forecast-accuracy summary generated at 10:31 AM EDT October 6 was consulted. Kentucky overnight ranges were shifted lower using the recommended KDVK and KLEX low-temperature corrections. Upstate lows were widened downward for KLQK without applying its full correction to Clemson and KCEU. HRRR received the most weight among scored models, while RAP received less weight because of its smaller sample and larger error. Friday ranges were widened because 72-hour range coverage remains 46.4%.

The low-probability precipitation bin has observed precipitation slightly more often than forecast, so small residual probabilities were retained even where official deterministic guidance is dry. Weekend tropical-remnant rain begins beyond these three forecast days and is described as context, not as a Friday hazard. This candidate does not modify the repository, forecast archive, website or widget.

appliedAdjustments.details: Lowered the overnight ranges using the recommended KDVK -2.5°F and KLEX -1.5°F low-temperature corrections while retaining enough width for the rural-to-urban spread. Daytime guidance was not bias-shifted because the current high-temperature station biases remain below the correction threshold. Friday's range was widened because 72-hour coverage remains 46.4%.

Widened nighttime ranges downward to represent KLQK's recommended -3.5°F low-temperature correction without applying the full adjustment to Clemson or KCEU. No daytime station correction was applied because all Upstate high-temperature candidates are currently monitoring. HRRR received the greatest model weight; Friday's range was widened to cover the remaining GFS–ECMWF–NWS spread and weak 72-hour calibration.
